name: Henry the Navigator and Portuguese Exploration
summary: Prince Henry of Portugal, after participating in the capture of Ceuta (1415), became the patron of systematic maritime exploration. From his base at Sagres he sponsored annual voyages down the African coast, gathered cartographic knowledge, and introduced the caravel. His captains rounded Cape Bojador in 1434 (previously thought impassable) and explored to present-day Sierra Leone before his death in 1460. Henry's patronage inaugurated the Age of Discovery.
outcomes: School of navigation established at Sagres

_quarry.structural_significance: The systematic organization of exploration under crown patronage, Henry's model, became the template for all subsequent European maritime empires.

sources_used: Diffie & Winius, Foundations of the Portuguese Empire
